newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CA workers fight Bank Austria plan.
newsitem.headline: CA workers fight Bank Austria plan.

text.p: Creditanstalt employees turned out in force on Friday to protest at the proposed takeover of Austria's second biggest bank by market leader Bank Austria, fearing the deal would mean massive job losses.
Around 3,000 of the bank's 8,000-strong workforce crowded into the elegant cash hall of privatisation candidate Creditanstalt's Vienna headquarters.
They brandished flyers that read: "This is my bank" and unanimously passed a resolution slamming Bank Austria's ambitions to acquire the nation's most traditional financial institution.
"It is unimaginable that Bank Austria should control Creditanstalt...It is unacceptable that Creditanstalt workers alone should pay the price of synergy effects," the resolution said.

Bank Austria workers are protected from redundancy by a quirk in Austrian employment law that differentiates between the savings bank sector, to which Bank Austria belongs, and commercial banks like Creditanstalt.
Creditanstalt chief executive Guido Schmidt-Chiari, a bank employee for almost 30 years, told the cheering crowd: "This is not my bank but the bank for which I work."
He urged Finance Minister Viktor Klima to think long and hard before accepting Bank Austria's bid for the state's 70 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary shares.
"It is a question of quality. An institution will not survive international competition through size alone," he said.
Bank Austria and Creditanstalt would have a combined domestic market share of 25 percent in terms of assets and would control around 70 percent of commercial banking activities.
